descriptionChirho: To close or shut up physically, especially of God closing the heavens or the womb, preventing rain or fertility.
To restrain, hold back, or check a person or force from acting, including stopping plagues and curbing behavior.
Nifal passive: to be stopped, restrained, or brought to a halt, said especially of plagues, rain, or hostile forces.
To be shut up or confined as a prisoner or captive, often as a passive participle describing someone held in bondage.
To detain someone, preventing them from departing; to urge someone to stay or hold them in place.
To retain, keep hold of, or preserve something in one's possession or control.
Idiomatic usage meaning to have power or ability to do something, to prevail or be able.
